subject: hornedHunter
kind: god body portrait (plan 3.1: whole body, regal pose, variant 0, swatch 0)
prompt:
Image 1 is a grey clay maquette of this figure: follow its pose, its parts and its framing, the whole figure from head to foot filling the square as it does, seen three-quarter front from a little above. It is a crude blockout: take its pose, its parts and its framing, not its stubby proportions. Paint over it completely: no grey clay and no plain smooth shapes may remain. Image 2 is a style reference only: match its painting style, brushwork, candle lighting, rim light, muted colours and dark background. Do not copy its head-and-shoulders framing. The subject, its face, its headgear and every ornament must follow the description below exactly; do not copy the man, the helm, the horns, the fur or the trim from Image 2.

A full-length painted portrait of the Horned Hunter, a towering hunter-god who calls the wolves to the hunt, twice a man's height, in a regal pose: standing tall and still, the spear held upright beside it in the right hand with its butt on the ground, chin raised. Three-quarter front view, the body and the face turned slightly toward the right side of the image. Square image. Framing: the whole figure fills the height of the square: the top of the antlers about 6% from the top edge and the feet about 94% from the top, centred, with dark empty space around the silhouette. One figure only: no people, no worshippers, no other creatures, no text, no border, no frame, no signature, no logo.
Lighting: a single warm candle key light from the upper left, a dim warm fill, deep warm shadows, and a thin soft warm rim light along the antlers, the head, the shoulders and the mantle that separates the whole silhouette clearly from the background. As in the style reference, much of the figure falls into deep warm shadow: the candle picks out the upper left of the head, the shoulders and the chest, and the lower body and the far side sink into the dark; it is not evenly lit. Background: plain, unpatterned, very dark warm brown close to #1C1A17, with no objects, no landscape, no horizon and no floor: the dark background runs unbroken to the bottom edge, with only a faint soft shadow under the feet.
Medium: painterly oil on a wood panel, loose visible brushwork and soft edges as in the style reference, moderate detail, never a crisp, clean digital illustration; a strong readable silhouette: the shape of the antlers, the leaf mantle and the tall spear against the dark background must still read when the image is shrunk to 64 pixels.
Colors: muted and earthy. The one clear colour of the figure is its leaf mantle: cloth of a deep bottle green, the green of jade in shade, clearly coloured, never grey, slate, olive or yellow-green (#1F6A50), the Thornwood's colour. All metal is dull old gold (#C9A23E), darkened and worn. Nothing in the image glows. No other saturated area larger than a small clasp or trim.

Subject: Headgear: tall branching antlers growing from its brow. Face: a lean, fierce, bearded face; its skin is a deep brown like hide (#7A5638), painted with stripes of lichen grey-green (#909080) warpaint across the eyes and down the cheeks, the arms and the chest. Body: a powerful, lean body wearing a kilt and leggings of dark leather. Mantle: a long mantle of overlapping cloth leaves over the shoulders and down the back, cloth of a deep bottle green, the green of jade in shade, clearly coloured, never grey, slate, olive or yellow-green (#1F6A50), the Thornwood's colour. Weapon: a tall hunting spear with a long leaf-shaped blade of dull old gold (#C9A23E), darkened and worn on a dark ash-wood shaft. Proportions: tall and heroic, a towering figure with long legs (the legs about half of its height) and the head about one eighth of its height; never squat, stocky, short-legged or dwarf-like.
Paint it as described, the whole figure clearly in view; a little more weathered and ancient in its surfaces, with a heavier, more imposing stance.
